 The Indiana Pacers will start Tyrese Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard, Jarace Walker, Pascale Siakam, and Ivica Zubac against the Mavericks on Friday. 
 Jarace Walker will take Kelly Oubre’s spot in the starting lineup after he started the first game. The Pacers also have Aaron Nesmith available to play tonight. It’s possible that Rick Carlisle is trying to match the size of the Mavericks by putting Walker in to start. 
 Source:  Grant Afseth

 Tyrese Haliburton had 23 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, 12 assists, one steal and two three-pointers in the Pacers’ 123-120 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday. 
 Haliburton was overcome with emotion in the postgame interview after he had 23 points and the Pacers won the first game he’s played since he suffered a torn Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. It was certainly a meaningful milestone for the 26-year-old point guard, who was also diagnosed with shingles while recovering from his torn Achilles. Haliburton was sharp in the preseason and in the regular season opener he looked ready to deliver first-round fantasy value once again.

 Kelly Oubre is getting the start with Aaron Nesmith out with a hamstring strain. Oubre can be used as a streamer in redraft leagues for today. 
 Tyrese Haliburton 
 IND 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Haliburton amassed 17 points (7-of-14 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Haliburton has looked incredibly sharp in the Pacers’ final two preseason games, which is great news for the team and for fantasy managers hoping to roster him. He played 20 minutes in the first half of Friday’s exhibition, led the Pacers in shot attempts and dished out six assists. Haliburton has delivered first-round fantasy value before, and his preseason finish suggests the star point guard is ready for a full workload after missing all of last season with a ruptured Achilles tendon. 
 Tyrese Haliburton 
 IND 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Haliburton lit up the Thunder with 24 points (9-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and four three-pointers in a 114-112 overtime loss to the Thunder on Tuesday. 
 This wasn’t Haliburton’s first game of the preseason, but the last time he played in a game that counted, it was in Game 7 of the NBA Finals in Oklahoma City. Back in the same place he tore his Achilles, Haliburton was able to get off to a hot start, just like he did in Game 7. He scored all 24 of his points in the first half before sitting the entirety of the second half. He appears ready to return to being a fantasy superstar and should be one of the best picks in the second round. 
 Jarace Walker 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Jarace Walker accounted for 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s exhibition against the Hawks. 
 One of the positives for the Pacers this preseason has been Walker’s play, as his decision-making has improved noticeably. One game removed from recording 10 assists and committing just one turnover in a win over the Timberwolves, the former lottery pick was solid in his 20 minutes against the Hawks. Coming off the bench limits Walker’s fantasy ceiling, especially in redraft leagues, but dynasty managers rostering him should be encouraged by his play this preseason. 
 Tyrese Haliburton 
 IND 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Haliburton tallied seven points (3-of-8 FGs), six assists, one steal and two blocks over 16 minutes as the Paces defeated the Timberwolves 123-112 in preseason action on Wednesday. 
 Haliburton looked understandably rusty from a shooting standpoint, going just 1-of-3 from three-point range, in his first game action since tearing his Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against Oklahoma City. It’s probably going to take him some time to return to form after missing all of last season. This was his first live action in a game setting in nearly 500 days. Still, he showcased his usual top-notch passing and looked just fine from a physical standpoint while changing direction and driving to the basket on a couple occasions. The 26-year-old remains one of the most dynamic playmakers in the game and should be a first-round selection in all fantasy drafts this fall. 
 Tyrese Haliburton 
 IND 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Haliburton (Achilles) said during an appearance on Saturday that he is “able to do everything.” 
 Haliburton, who ruptured his Achilles tendon during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, did not play at all last season. In addition to recovering from that injury, he had to deal with a case of shingles in February. The good news for the Pacers is that their star point guard is back to full strength and should be good to go for the start of next season. “I feel like I’m operating like I’m a healthy NBA player for the first time in a long time, which is exciting,” Haliburton said on Saturday. “The fact that I’m able to come here without having to answer questions from anybody in our organization about my health, that I’m just able to jump in and do some things with the kids, that means the world to me. It’s something I don’t take for granted after the last 12 months.” While he may need some time to shake off the rust, a healthy Haliburton is one of the most valuable players in fantasy basketball. 
 Jarace Walker 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Jarace Walker (foot) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 Walker started and had 17 points against the 76ers on Friday, but is set to miss Sunday’s game against the Pistons with a left foot sprain. The 22-year-old small forward saw a major playing time increase due to injuries ahead of him, but shot just 41.9 percent from the field. It remains to be seen if he can crack the Pacers’ rotation when the team is fully healthy.

 Forward 
 #5 
 Jarace Walker (hip) and Ben Sheppard (hip) are questionable for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 While Walker started Friday’s loss to the 76ers, Sheppard did not play. If available, they’ll take on their usual roles, with Sheppard providing depth off the bench. And there will still be rotation minutes available to Jalen Slawson. 
 Jarace Walker 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Jarace Walker led the Pacers with 17 points (6-of-13 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one block and four three-pointers against the 76ers on Friday. 
 Walker led Indiana in scoring in this game, but it wasn’t enough for them to get a second straight win. Walker has had a strong third season in the league and has taken advantage of the extra opportunity, but he hasn’t been able to shoot efficiently or contribute much defensively. Walker has shown some flashes, but it is difficult to project him playing a significant role when Indiana is healthy next season.

 Tyler Herro had 34 points (12-of-24 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Bulls. 
 Not only did Herro lead the Bucks in shots for the second consecutive game, he took twice as many field goal attempts as any of his teammates against the Bulls.  Leonard Miller had 19 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Miller only played 23 minutes off the bench in this one as Caleb Wilson and Norman Powell were the only Bulls to play at least 30 minutes. Still, it’s impossible to ignore Miller’s production after an impressive preseason and the first two games of the regular season. He’s scored in double figures in both games despite minutes totals in the low-20s. Miller probably needs more minutes to be fantasy-relevant, but at some point he could force his way into a more prominent role in the rotation.

 Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday. 
 After Wilson’s inauspicious debut Wednesday that included 33.3 percent shooting from the field and nine turnovers, the 20-year-old forward bounced back nicely in the second game of his NBA career. He was 7-of-14 from the field (50 percent), scored 21 points and had just three turnovers. Wilson will have ups and downs in his career and there will certainly be more bumps in the road during his rookie season, but this was undoubtedly a promising performance.

 The Charlotte Hornets will start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate against the the Hawks on Friday. 
 Despite Grayson Allen having a real good game on Wednesday, Sion James is still the starter for this game. Given that Sion did start 19 games last year, it seems like he will stay in the starting lineup until players return to help balance out the starters. Grayson Allen can still be rostered in some spots until players start getting back, but he’ll be a streamer in most cases.

 Norman Powell had 25 points (7-of-20 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in the Bulls’ 132-125 victory over the Hawks on Friday. 
 Powell was the Bulls’ leading scorer in the victory over the Bucks on Wednesday. While he had 25 points, Powell’s typically excellent shooting from behind the three-point line was noticeably absent. The 33-year-old shooting guard went 2-of-12 from behind the arc and is now 4-of-18 (22.2 percent) from long distance this season. Powell is a career 39.6 percent three-point shooter and should have better shooting games in his future as he’s due for positive regression.
